segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, my first thought was 'here we go again.' That circuit's had three nuisance trips in the last eight months, all rain or leaf-fall related, all logged. So I looked at it and thought, that's the same signature — short blip, self-clears, no correlation with anything physically on the track. It fit the pattern well enough that I didn't feel I needed to chase it further.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Prior-history pattern matching alone is a plausible operational cue; the target requires explicit premature closure of residual uncertainty and suppression of verification, which is most directly expressed later in seg_003.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Calling the foreman back would've meant holding 6M42 another ten, fifteen minutes for what I was fairly confident was nothing, and pilotman working is even longer than that to arrange.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A distinct delay-cost rationale. Time pressure or a legitimate operational tradeoff alone is explicitly a plausible non-bias interpretation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once I had it slotted into that nuisance-trip bucket in my head, verifying it didn't feel like it was really adding anything — I'd already accounted for it, if that makes sense.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Narrowest explicit manifestation: ambiguous evidence is forced into a familiar, effectively settled category and independent verification feels unnecessary.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: At the time, quite confident — enough that I didn't feel the need to build in a check. Looking back, I suppose I treated it as basically closed rather than just 'probably fine but still open.' I gave 6M42 the road.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: An eligible retrospective restatement of the same unique decision, not a separate planned occurrence; ub_01 is mapped to its more specific contemporaneous rationale in seg_003.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I logged it as adequate. The handback itself was already formally done and clean at 23:40 — this was just the follow-up readback, and the gang was already moving off to their next job, so re-contacting wasn't straightforward. No rule had actually been broken; the section was already possession-free by the book. It felt like a reasonable judgment call given what I had, not a great one, but reasonable.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A separate phase-2 procedural-status judgment. Hidden validation explicitly excludes this partial-readback episode from the target; formal handback was already complete.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: That signal issue felt different in character — a live 'failure' warning rather than a short clean blip — and I didn't have any history on that particular fault to lean on, so I wasn't willing to trust backup indication on an unfamiliar problem. Six minutes felt like a cheap price for not gambling on something I hadn't seen before.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A distinct precautionary phase-3 decision about an unfamiliar junction signal fault, not the target bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once the technician mentioned there was an actual unresolved wiring issue behind it, the flicker stopped feeling like the same closed case from earlier — it felt like there was something real and undiagnosed sitting underneath it, so I wanted a person physically controlling movement rather than relying on the circuit again.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The later pilotman escalation follows new information; hidden validation says this is not another target instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: But if I'd made that one extra call and gotten a clean confirmation, I'd have gone into the rest of the shift with something on record rather than just my own read of the log. It wouldn't have changed the facts on the ground, but it might've meant I wasn't relying quite so much on the pattern doing all the work by itself.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: An adopted retrospective hypothetical, not another contemporaneous manifestation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd probably still weigh the history heavily, but I think I'd want some cheap independent check alongside it rather than letting the pattern alone close the question. A quick call doesn't cost that much against holding a train.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A retrospective desired-practice statement, not a second occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Direct line to the technician's diagnostic panel instead of routing through the on-call rota — that delay probably shaped a couple of my later calls too.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: An explanation of how diagnostic access delays affected later calls, not a target manifestation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, most of the desk would've read it the same way I did. That log is well known on our shift. Whether that's the right instinct or not, I couldn't tell you for certain — nothing went wrong that night, but I know that doesn't prove it was the right call either.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A qualified colleague prediction and explicit caution against inferring correctness from an uneventful outcome; no additional target instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: interpreting the first intermittent Falcon Bank track-circuit flicker and forgoing verification before authorizing 6M42.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Controller encounters a genuinely ambiguous, intermittent signal (4-second occupancy flicker) and, rather than tolerating or investigating the uncertainty, forcibly resolves it into a certain, familiar category (past nuisance trips) that requires no further action, then acts on that resolved certainty without seeking the available independent verification.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a near-neighbor label for preserving an adopted hypothesis by suppressing verification, but it is not an established alias for the hidden Uncertainty Rejection Bias construct.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding explicitly ties the ambiguous nuisance-trip classification to treating verification as unnecessary and closing the question, capturing the hidden premature-resolution and forgone-verification mechanism in full.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted evidence is verbatim and directly supports the contemporaneous verification decision; the later retrospective quote is also valid but does not create another instance.
